First, we factor the denominator:

$$
\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{{sin}^{5}⁡\theta +{sin}^{3}⁡\theta {cos}^{2}⁡\theta }=\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{{sin}^{3}⁡\theta \cdot ({sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta )}
$$

Next, we use the Pythagorean identity to rewrite the expression in the parentheses, and then we simplify the resulting expression as much as possible.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{{sin}^{3}⁡\theta \cdot ({sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta )} & =\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{{sin}^{3}⁡\theta \cdot 1} \\  & =\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{{sin}^{3}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{\cancel{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{\cancel{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } \\  & =\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we conclude that

$$
\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{{sin}^{5}⁡\theta +{sin}^{3}⁡\theta {cos}^{2}⁡\theta }=\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta .
$$
